#3229. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”

Phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to plan, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” says Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images

Once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to plan, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR

“It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR

Once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”

Probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA

During the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel says. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

Andrew Jones is a freelance journalist based near Helsinki. He writes about the space industry and technology with a particular focus on China's activities.

#3228. Devo Bring ‘Whip It’ to Thanksgiving Day Parade

Q: Are they not ad men? A: They are Devo! The long-running New Wave group whipped a bevy of energy-domed dancers into a frenzy to the sounds of “Whip It” on Saturday while stumping for GEICO on a Thanksgiving Day parade float.

Devo, perhaps the unlikeliest of performers in the parade’s 100-year history, delivered their 1980 hit while a giant inflatable turkey hovered overhead.

“Whip It” was the song that changed everything for Devo. The group originally formed at Kent State University a few years after the Kent State Massacre almost as a response to violence with absurdity. Their name is a cutesy take on “devolution,” the idea that mankind was regressing. They put out two excellent albums of artsy post-punk before recording “Whip It” for their 1980 album, Freedom of Choice. Thanks to a clever video that MTV played repeatedly in its infancy, they became superstars.

“Before it, the record company ignored us,” the band’s Mark Mothersbaugh told Rolling Stone in 2018. “Then ‘Whip It’ came and they made millions of dollars and they’re like, ‘Oh, these weirdos can actually make money.’ So it became a thing where they started interfering and going, ‘Hey, if there’s anything you guys need, we’ll help you. Just write another ‘Whip It.””

“The reason why we made the video that way was because every DJ we encountered was like, ‘Hey guys, whip it,’ and they’d make the jerkoff move,” the band’s Gerry Casale said in the same interview. “And at first, I was trying to tell them, ‘No, no. It was inspired by [author] Thomas Pynchon.’ And their faces would drop and lose interest immediately, bummed out. Trending Stories In Praise of Andrew Scott Raye Opens Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade With 'Joy' Watch Miranda Lambert Perform Medley of Her Hits at Dallas Cowboys Halftime Show Watch 'Sesame Street' Pay Homage to Mariah Carey’s 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'

“So we thought, ‘Let’s do exactly what they profanely think this was all about,'” he continued. “Mark and I collected lots of novelty stuff and quack books, and I found a men’s magazine from the Fifties or Sixties with a feature about a guy who was a Hollywood stuntman. He left the business and bought a dude ranch in Arizona. His wife was a stripper in the local clubs on Sunset Boulevard so when people would stay at the dude ranch, he had this routine where he whipped his wife’s clothes off in the corral as entertainment. They developed this act and whipped her down to her underwear. The article had pictures and the whole thing. We went, ‘OK, we’re gonna do this.’ There’s so many politically incorrect things in that video, it’s hard to count.”

It is unclear if GEICO was aware of this story.

The 9-to-5 desk job can leave you feeling stiff, hunched and full of tension in your shoulders and spine, so you'll need to focus on moving throughout the day to help ease this. But there are also some desk exercises you can do if you're short on time, and they'll help correct posture and release that sore, tight feeling in your mid-to-upper back.

These six beginner-friendly posture exercises come from Dr. Sammy Fit, who recommends trying them if you sit for long periods and need a quick reset. She's a licensed doctor of physical therapy with a B.S. in Exercise Science who wants you to "discover functional fitness while preventing injuries." Check them out below.

While these exercises are recommended by a qualified physical therapist, you should always listen to your body and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or tingling. Working with a physical therapist, physician, or similar professional will help you determine the issue and provide specialized recommendations based on your personal journey.

While you don't get given sets or reps for these moves, I'd try starting with 60 seconds of each, or 6-8 reps per side per exercise, and 2 sets. Move slowly, with control, focusing on your shoulders, spine, chest and mid-upper back area.

Try to hold, lean and twist into the moves to get the most from each exercise, and don't be afraid to breathe as you hold uncomfortable positions. Keep your neck and gaze neutral so that you avoid putting pressure on your cervical spine (the back of the neck).

#3223. AI Agents Are Testing the Limits of Zero-Trust Security

As autonomous AI agents work together, verifying their actions, enforcing security policies, and maintaining accountability becomes increasingly difficult

Vishal Sharma is a Reader in the School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Science at Queen's University Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.

In a de-authentication attack on an aerial vehicle using a human- and agent-in-the-loop approach, an AI agent can quickly scan the active channel and autonomously intercept traffic, thus reducing the time to react and regain control.

This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast.

Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.

However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?

There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?

Having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.

This opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution.

Another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust.

An in-house experiment done at Queen’s University Belfast (QUB) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system.

There is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals?

Our team worked around this space, which at first involved demonstrating that the problem exists, and its impact and scale can be huge when you must prove trust under boundaries of asynchronous autonomy. Solutions towards such problems can be simplified by keeping things like AI-bill of material or leveraging distributed ledger technology that can provide underlying infrastructure of trust via traceability and immutability and keep the agentic activity and associated trust vectors agnostic to the platform.

Within trust, another factor that is not well explored but needs a thorough investigation is the concept of horizontal anomalies. It defines how agents interact differently with various sources under different settings. As agents behave correctly and align themselves with the architectural expectations for one specific task or application, that does not necessarily mean these can be trusted for their operations across all associated components. How to identify such anomalies and what methods can be employed without complying with such agents remain open questions and topics for further exploration.

The critical aspect is that utility of agents with semi to low trust governance offer short-term high benefits, but the cost of recovery when the system fails is yet to be explored, and this will not be a contained issue. We are looking into the system where agents are already sweeping into different entities and may not allow complete recovery. For example, a mere supply chain issue because an agent going rogue is now not a containable small task but needs sweeping across all the touch points of those affected agents. This essentially means despite the number of agents and their ability to trigger proxy-agents, which may not be directly linked to the wider ecosystem, there is a need to ensure that computationally expensive trackers are in place for all the agents.

Other relevant PhD works carried out in our research group are towards sovereignty of AI, exploring aspects of trust and accountability. Our hypothesis is that sovereignty and trust need to be governed together as onus of provenance is high on the host of agents. Thus, it needs understanding of laws governing trust-based executions of AI. The important challenge here is that there is a vital difference between missed information and missed instructions, and both have different impacts when it comes to trusted accountability.

The real-world issue with these systems lies in the failure to adopt approaches that historically have relied on state-based modeling when governing trust. In stateless systems where agentic autonomy is high, the convergence and reliability towards trust-provenance decreases significantly. Thus, it brings us back to the original question – does a true zero-trust even exist?

Can policies be trusted? If so, how should these be managed without falling into the trap of policy-based accessibility and control issues? Despite the argument that PEP can help manage access between the agents, placing a single entity and expecting it to scale towards all agentic interactions is underestimating the problem space.

Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models.

To build our case and settle around the challenges of trust embeddings in Agentic AI, within Cyber AI hub, we are exploring opportunities to help companies scale up as well as build their pipeline of agentic applications for commercial viability. However, the element that governs our regular work and decision making are scale of problem and number of agentic deployments, anomaly detection across the agentic workflows, continuous evaluation of the attack surfaces and vulnerability assessment, exploring differences in the pure agentic AI and task-driven multi-agent system.

We are working with industries where trust is a pre-requisite, and these organizations put trust as a guardrail managed via internal policies with a pure focus on securing the systems through policies rather than trusting the third-party agentic service providers. Additionally, trust in services is presented by ensuring constraints around their service models where agentic activities are tracked and managed via logs including management of their token revocation list to avoid replay attacks depending on the type of application. Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models. Things like balancing the adversarial accuracy along with certified adversarial robustness can help to determine how much the model can be trusted.

But the question is, can we settle for anything less than foolproof when it comes to deployment of agents in the real world? And if so, how much impact can be controlled, and who is responsible for the remaining component?

When it comes to safely navigating natural disasters, knowledge is power. Wherever you live geographically, it is important to know what threats you are up against and what it means to be prepared. If you live in a region of the world that experiences earthquakes, earthquake alert alarms are easy-to-install tools that help give you a more advanced warning of the impending event.

While earthquake alert alarms are not a substitute for following local warnings and evacuation orders, they are complementary tools. The best earthquake alert alarms work by detecting the P-wave (compression wave) of an earthquake, which travels faster than the more destructive S-wave (shear wave). This technology allows for the detection of earthquakes that occur miles away.

Having a properly-installed earthquake alert alarm can make the difference between having enough time to escape to safety and having to endure the earthquake from where you are. The best earthquake alert alarms also function as SOS lights that can help you flag down rescuers.

#3220. Apple has iPads running macOS already, but don’t get too excited

With iPads running the same chips as Macs, many have wished Apple would give us the option of running macOS on them instead of the somewhat clunky iPadOS windowing system. Apple’s previous arguments against converging devices have been somewhat weakened by the launch of the touchscreen MacBook Pro.

A new report says that Apple already has iPads running macOS internally, and that work on a giant iPad continues, but don’t hold your breath for a public launch of either …

As iPad hardware has grown more powerful over the years, the software has struggled to keep up. We saw split-screen capabilities first, with full windowing finally coming to the devices in iPadOS 26 last year.

The UI is still rather clunky compared to macOS, however, leading a significant number of people to wish that Apple simply offered the option of using the more powerful operating system on its tablet devices.

I would be comfortable with 11" and 13" devices running macOS. Actually, I don’t require them to run macOS itself, but I do need them to run macOS apps. I wish the iPad could match a MacBook’s productivity. Running macOS on an iPad seems like a reasonable idea. The MacBook Air is now the better price choice, while those needing a powerhouse will always choose a MacBook Pro or Studio.

Some suggest that running macOS on iPad would reduce Mac sales, but I disagree. I own a nearly full-spec MacBook Pro 16" and expect to keep a machine like that, yet I also purchased a MacBook Air for lighter travel. I would prefer an iPad over the Air, but I cannot choose it because it lacks the apps I require. If it supported them, I would buy the iPad Pro with all accessories, and Apple would gain more revenue from me. I appreciate the concept of owning an iPad, but currently it lacks the value needed to justify paying more for a device that simply does less than a MacBook Air.

In a podcast Q&A, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says that Apple is already doing this internally, but there’s no sign of any plans to make it available outside the company.

Apple has iPads internally running macOS, and they’ve had that for some time. The fact that they have the underlying architecture of Apple Silicon that’s the same on the iPad and the Mac gives them the flexibility in order to test these types of things.

In terms if they’re actually going to do it – would they bring macOS to the iPad itself – at this point I don’t think that’s going to happen anytime soon. I’ve checked into this and there’s no ongoing operating system project right now in terms of a brand new operating system for the iPad – there is no work being done to consumerize macOs on the iPad.

Gurman says Apple seems set to continue to make piecemeal changes over time to bring iPad capabilities closer to those of the Mac but is showing no signs of full convergence.

He reiterated that work on a long-rumored giant-sized folding iPad continues.

The other thing I want to say is that I’m really excited for this potential of Project J312. That is, this giant 19-inch, 20-inch foldable iPad. And it’s basically like a gigantic iPhone Duo with no display on the outside.

However, he says there’s no guarantee it will ever launch, saying the timings have already slipped from 2027 through 2028 to 2029, but both cost and yield issues may still kill the project. If it does launch, it’s expected to cost anywhere from $3,000 to $5,000.

These models are a generation behind Amazon's current lineup: The company introduced redesigned Paperwhite and Colorsoft models (plus accessories) in October, with the new Paperwhite now starting at $199.99, and replaced the 2024 Scribe with a third-generation model in December 2025. As for its “like-new” label, it means these are pre-owned devices that Amazon certified to look and work like new.

The Like-New Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $161.99 from $224.99, almost 30% off. For that price, you're doubling the storage of a standard Paperwhite and getting wireless charging, an ad-free lock screen, and a front light that automatically adjusts to your surroundings—on top of the same sharp seven-inch display, IPX8 water resistance, and up to 12 weeks of battery life as the standard Paperwhite, as noted by this PCMag review.

The Like-New Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (32GB) is down to $179.99 from $287.99, almost 40% off. And for that price, you're getting twice the storage for a standard Colorsoft, which is particularly useful for comics, manga, and graphic novels that take up more space than regular ebooks, along with wireless charging, an automatically adjusting front light, and an ad-free lock screen. However, as PCMag notes in its review, the color display produces more subdued tones than a conventional tablet, so the Paperwhite remains the more economical choice if you primarily read novels.

The Like-New Kindle Scribe (16GB) is down to $251.99 from $359.99, the biggest dollar discount in this roundup. Unlike the other Kindles here, it's built for reading and writing, with a 10.2-inch, 300ppi glare-free display and a Premium Pen with an eraser and shortcut button—making it the most versatile option for readers who want an e-reader that doubles as a digital notebook.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then shows how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

#3213. iOS 27.3 introduces design changes for these Apple apps

iOS 27.3 includes many new features for Apple’s built-in apps, but it also introduces design changes on the iPhone across Calendar, Safari, Music, and more. Here’s what’s new.

Apple is always iterating on the design of its software. While major overhauls like iOS 26’s Liquid Glass don’t come along often, the company makes smaller design changes all the time via software updates. In iOS 27.3, which will launch to all users next month, Apple has design changes coming to four popular apps: Health, Calendar, Safari, and Music.

The Health app gets the biggest design changes.

As seen above, Health introduces brand new Insights, Longevity, and Browse tabs that replace the previous options and include a variety of fresh UI elements like a top navigation row, personalized prompts and coaching, educational videos, and a lot more.

Apple Calendar’s design updates focus on making key buttons more reachable one-handed.

As the side-by-side above shows, the buttons for search and creating a new event have moved out of the top-right corner and into the bottom of the screen.

Calendar also now shows the year at the top of the screen next to the current month, and has updated the ‘Today’ button to show the current date instead.

Safari introduces an optional new design for tabs: Vertical Tabs. You can enable these inside Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari for a different approach to tabs across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. Here’s an example of vertical tabs on iPhone Duo.

Vertical Tabs won’t be for everyone, but they’ve proven popular in other browsers, so it’s great to see Safari add the option.

Apple Music has a subtle but beautiful design update in iOS 27.3 when viewing lyrics in landscape mode.

Song artwork is now able to break the constraints of a square and blend seamlessly into the scrolling lyrics view. Here are examples from Beta Profiles on X:

New in iOS 27.3 Beta: Animated artwork blends into the Apple Music player in landscape mode, and it looks so good. pic.twitter.com/k8rgSEALGo

This lyrics view was previously available on iPhone Duo, but now it’s coming to all iPhones.

#3211. These Signature Sony Headphones Are Under $200 During Black Friday

The Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones are the most recent entry in Sony's 1000X series, which has been around since 2016. They're the best over-ear headphones in terms of audio quality currently on the market—but not everyone can (or needs to) drop nearly half a grand on headphones.

The WH-1000XM5 are a generation older and were at the top of their class until they were supplanted by the XM6. On the plus side, by virtue of being older, they're currently discounted to $198 (down from the original $399.99) during Amazon's early Black Friday sale. That 50% off brings it down to the lowest price they've ever reached, a good deal for premium headphones that still sound incredible, even in 2026.

I have been a loyal customer of the 1000X line for many years; they're my go-to headphones for most activities. The WH-1000XM5 received an "outstanding" review from PCMag for their top-notch audio quality and exceptional audio when using the best-in-class active noise cancellation. The headphones are also well-designed to be comfortable for long listening sessions. The ear controls use tapping and swiping, which isn't my favorite, but it's what all modern headphones are moving toward. There's a companion app that lets you adjust your EQ settings to your liking, including what the swiping and tapping functions do.

These headphones also have a stereo 3.5mm connection, which is perfect for those who want to use a cable and not worry about battery life. And speaking of battery life, Sony says you can expect about 30 hours, but it will vary depending on your use of ANC. They are compatible with AAC, LDAC, and SBC codecs and have multipoint connection, meaning you can pair them with more than one device at the same time.

Personally, I think the value for the money you get with the XM5 for $198 is better than paying full price for the XM6. If you're looking to get ahead of the Black Friday chaos and secure an amazing deal on great headphones, this is it.

As the weather conditions change, property maintenance becomes a constant battle against the elements. From stray branches to scattered yard debris, picking up fallen leaves often feels like an endless task.

But what happens if it’s your neighbor’s leaves that keep falling onto your driveway or front yard? Who is responsible for the cleanup? And what is the best way to approach your neighbor about it? This is especially true if your car is covered with leaves as a result.

Just as rules and proper etiquette apply to trimming back overhanging branches, they also apply to managing shared property boundaries.

To help navigate this awkward issue, I asked experts to clarify the rules regarding fallen leaves from a neighbor's trees and the most effective ways to raise this with them.

Here's what they say and top tips to avoid a neighborhood dispute.

While it’s a normal occurrence, clearing your neighbor’s leaves off your own driveway can be frustrating, but what do you do?

According to legal experts, your first step should be identifying the exact origin of the falling leaves.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

“Investigate why the leaves are being deposited on your land,” states Roger Diefendorf, attorney at Forum & Lex, P.C. “Is it due to natural shedding or wind? Or is your neighbor or their gardener using their hosepipe to deposit leaves onto your drive?

As a general rule, I would discuss with the adjoining owner to reach a sensible solution

“This will affect whether or not you can justify requesting that the behaviour be ceased. As a general rule, this would be something I would discuss with the adjoining owner to reach a sensible solution.”

Another top tip is to identify who owns the trees shedding the leaves. In many cases, larger trees along street borders fall under the jurisdiction of your local municipal government. In that case, you can reach out to your local city services department (calling 311) to request assistance.

Although it may feel unfair, property owners are generally responsible for removing debris that ends up on their own land/property.

“Leaves on someone else's land would reasonably be expected to be cleared by the owner of that land,” states Jonathan Carcone, Principal of 4 Brothers Buy Houses. “If damage were likely to occur or did occur, it would be sensible to take photographs, ideally with a legible date.”

However, if you find your neighbor’s trees are encroaching on your property, it’s always worth having a friendly word with next door.

Of course, the occasional leaf cleanup probably won’t get you a sympathetic reaction. But if you are dealing with a persistent issue or problematic trees, what’s the best approach? And how do you keep it civil without falling out with your neighbors?

“Talk to your neighbor about the problem, explaining what would be an acceptable solution,” suggests Diefendorf. “ It may be helpful to suggest something such as:

‘I have quite a lot of leaves accumulating against my front door and in the drains. Would this be something you would be willing to agree with me on each fall?’”

“Leaves blown across to your property by a neighbor's gardener may be beyond their knowledge. You may wish to point this out and ask them to speak to their gardener.

"Be as amicable as possible, being clear as to what you would wish them to do. Once satisfied with an arrangement, it would be sensible to put something in writing setting out the agreed action. ”

Essentially, preventing legal conflicts is always the best course, and friendly agreement maintains good relationships. Plus, having helpful neighbors is, after all, invaluable.

For more top tips on reusing fallen leaves in your yard, check out the free fall hack that stops weeds in their tracks.

This Greenworks leaf blower delivers 770cfm/180mph of power with a runtime of 60 minutes, and a rapid recharge of one hour. It offers a variable-speed trigger, as well as cruise control for precision cleaning, so you can swap between heavy and light cleanups.

#3204. Major MacBook Air ‘overhaul’ could launch next year, per Gurman

Apple has a new MacBook Air with M6 chip coming early next year, but per Mark Gurman on his latest podcast episode, a “big MacBook Air overhaul” could launch as early as 2027 too. Here’s what he said.

Today on the latest episode of Mark Gurman’s Power On podcast, the well-sourced reporter answered a listener question that involves the future of the MacBook Air.

When asked about the next-generation MacBook Air, here’s what Gurman said:

The next MacBook Air project, J913 and J915, the 13-inch version and the 15-inch version, that is coming in spring 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2. And this is going to be another “chip and ship,” so a chip refresh.

And we are getting to the end of the road here for the current MacBook Air design. The current MacBook Air design was introduced in ’22, was refreshed in ’23 with the 15-inch model. We’re now in 2027. MacBook Air is Apple’s most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027-2028 is when we’re going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation.

There are several noteworthy takeaways here:

It would be unusual for Apple to launch two distinct MacBook Air models in the same calendar year. However, if that does happen, it would follow the exact same playbook Apple used with the MacBook Pro this year.

Of course it's getting an 'overhaul' (whatever that means for a MacBook that will largely look and work the exact same) because it needs to replace the MacBook Pros pricing structure. Now that the Neo exists, the Air line needs to be exponentially more expensive because that's how Apple operates these days. Give you the absolute bare bones minimum at a huge premium and then absolutely soak anyone who needs anything of value.

This March, a new MacBook Pro launched with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips but the same design that’s been around since 2021. Then in October, Apple unveiled the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display and a new industrial design.

It sounds like a very similar rollout could happen for the MacBook Air in 2027.

#3203. ‘The Challenge’ Alum Tyler Duckworth’s Cause Of Death Revealed

We now have the official cause of death for MTV’s The Challenge alum Tyler Duckworth.

The reality TV personality died from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, the North Dakota State Forensic Examiner’s Office confirmed to Deadline. His manner of death was ruled natural.

The Sun, which first reported his death, revealed Duckworth was found unresponsive in his bathroom on August 11 and was subsequently pronounced dead. The publication cited officials in North Dakota as saying the death was classified as unattended, meaning there were no witnesses there at the time.

His mother, Joni, announced her son’s death on Facebook. “My son, Tyler, passed away earlier this week,” she wrote. “Cause of death has yet to be determined. I will post on Facebook about services as soon as his dad and I figure it out.”

Hypertensive cardiovascular disease refers to a group of heart and blood vessel conditions caused by long-term, unmanaged high blood pressure.

Duckworth first appeared on MTV’s The Real World: Key West and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge, winning twice.

His death came nearly two weeks after he appeared at The Challenge Mania event on July 31 in Minneapolis. He posted a photo of himself alongside fellow Challenge alums on Instagram on August 2.

“@challengemaniapodcast always knows how to bring the BEST of the BEST together!!, he wrote at the time. “So proud to represent my hometown of Minneapolis along with these other challenge legends. The fans are what keep us coming out! Hearing your stories of courage, inspiration & joy that you’ve got being a fan of the franchise is humbling each and every time. Also, pretty sure we nailed the cast photo for the lost season of The Real World: Minneapolis!! Thank you Minneapolis!”

Duckworth appeared on The Real World: Key West in 2006 and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge – The Duel, The Gauntlet III, Cutthroat, Rivals, All Stars 2 and All Stars 3 — winning Cutthroat and Rivals. On Cutthroat, he won a bruising, 40-minute elimination round against heavy hitter CT Tamburello after Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio was eliminated in what has been remember as the “Bananas Backpack” match. After 10 years, he returned to the franchise for All Stars 2.

After his run on reality TV, Duckworth became a middle school and high school teacher and was actively pursuing a doctorate degree, according to an interview with Entertainment Weekly.

#3202. The Sonos Arc Ultra Soundbar Is $250 Off During Black Friday

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

Amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out our comprehensive Black Friday coverage.

For those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to plan around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a big step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a new Sound Motion driver that it says doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

The best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

#3201. Festivitas brings holiday cheer to your Mac with snow you can shovel

Back in 2024, developer Simon Støvring launched Festivitas, an app that brings a ton of holiday cheer to your Mac. This year, the app is getting even more whimsical and delightful with new snowfall features.

For those unfamiliar, Festivitas lets you hang lights of different colors and patterns from your Mac’s menu bar and dock. It has a bunch of different customization options, so you can tweak the lights to match your preferences.

Last year, the app added a new snowfall effect alongside those Christmas lights, plus Shortcuts integration and a dedicated iPhone and iPad app with customizable widgets.

This year’s Festivitas update expands that snowfall feature. Now, the snow that falls from the top of your Mac’s screen can pile up at the bottom of your screen, and you can use your mouse to shovel it away. This joins the existing ability to adjust snow amount, flake size, fall speed, and wind direction.

Head to the Festivitas website to get started and bring some holiday cheer to your Apple devices.

It's not on sale, but it's the biggest game in the world right now, so we had to include it here. The long-awaited follow-up to GTA 5 is the most impressive game in the series and a technical showcase that raises the bar for open-world games. The expansive Vice City setting and myriad activities offer countless hours of crime-fueled mayhem, while the intriguing characters keep you invested in the narrative. Stellar Blade is a hack-and-slash action-adventure game in the best spirit of the genre. It takes full advantage of the PS5's horsepower and serves up thrilling combat sequences and an engaging story. The graphics aren't half bad-looking, either.

Long before Elden Ring, Bloodborne and Dark Souls, From Software released Demon's Souls, the first Souls title to truly establish the core gameplay loop that has taken the gaming world by storm. For the current generation, Sony had Bluepoint develop this faithful, beautiful remaster, which improves on the original title and updates it with amazing graphics, new weapons, and items.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor thanks to its larger scope, both narratively and gameplay-wise. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer a deep level of customization.

Sony’s standard PS5 pad remains one of the best controllers around thanks to its responsive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers. Standard colorways, including white, midnight black, cosmic red, and galactic purple, are down to $54 here, beating PlayStation Direct’s sale price.

The Razer Raiju V3 Pro's TMR sticks offer precise control over movements while removing the risk of stick drift, and the gamepad’s Hall Effect triggers are fantastic too. The controller is highly customizable with removable back buttons and personalization via Windows and/or mobile software.

The PS5 is hard to come by this Black Friday, and if you do find one, it's at retail. That stings, but it doesn't hurt to get a PS5 when you can. This model is the base PS5 Slim, now the cheapest PS5 available. It comes with an 825GB SSD.

Here's a game that divided the Tom's Guide crew.

Some of us love it; some of us...not so much.

The consensus is that it's no Spider-Man, but it's still an entertaining and cinematic title with the typical graphical flair you'd expect from developer Insomniac Games. Personally, I skipped it, which was hard because I was looking forward to it. The negative impressions were enough to keep me from taking the plunge, but at $49, it might be worth grabbing now.

Naturally, as a tentpole title, it's been pricey up to now — but with $20 off for Black Friday / Cyber Monday, it's a much more tempting prospect. To let the claws out, or to keep them tucked away...

One of Tom's Guide's gaming experts, Tony Polanco, gave Control: Resonant a 4.5 out of 5 in our review, which is impressive because he was super hyped building up to the game's launch. All too often, when you're that hyped for a game, it fails to live up to your lofty expectations, but it still managed to surpass them.

"Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor thanks to its larger scope, both narratively and gameplay-wise. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer a deep level of customization. Aside from some confusing maps, this is an almost perfect action-based title," reads the Tom's Guide review. That's some high praise!

A lot of the games we've featured here are rated T or M. But what about those younger gamers?

Right now, you can save big on the PS5 version of the latest Lego Batman game. It's normally a full-priced $70 game, but Amazon has bumped $20 off the price for Black Friday / Cyber Monday.

Personally, I love playing any of the Lego games with my stepson, as they're wildly entertaining for him, but they still offer enough challenging elements to keep me entertained. Plus, there's the trademark adult humor hidden throughout that takes the experience up a notch while going right over the kid's head.

Turtle Beach makes some of the most popular gaming headsets, and the Stealth 600 is one of the company's best-reviewed options. It offers a mappable wheel and mode button that give you more customization while you play your favorite games.

The sound quality is solid, so you can expect details to come through whether you're playing the latest first-person shooters or immersive survival horror games. The 80-hour battery life is another huge benefit, since you won't need to worry about charging it after every gaming session.

If you’re tired of gaming headsets that feel like a medieval vice grip after an hour, the Sony Inzone H5 is a massive breath of fresh air.

Easily one of the best wireless picks for both PS5 and PC, it’s so featherweight and comfortable that you’ll genuinely forget it’s on your head — dangerous, considering its 28-hour battery life will easily outlast your snacks, your social life, and your best intentions of going to bed at a reasonable hour.

Under the hood, its 40mm drivers pump out crisp, detailed sound, while full 3D audio support means you’ll finally hear that camper creeping up behind you before you’re staring at a respawn screen.

From the halfway line! NBA 2K27 with an almighty shot of a Black Friday deal — taking the price down to under $30.

That's a massive 57% saving on what is a very dense game for the basketball fans out there. MyCAREER is filled with eras, animations are greatly improved and so much more.

It’s a basketball sandbox, and it’s better than half price.

I’ve played an absurd number of racing games this year, and I definitely didn’t have Star Wars: Galactic Racer being one of the year’s absolute bangers on my bingo card. Yet here we are.

The hook is brilliantly simple: it’s a roguelike arcade racer where you blitz through randomized gauntlets across different planets, bolting on new upgrades between runs to survive the next track. That extra tactical layer elevates what is already some seriously tight, chaotic racing gameplay.

Every time I boot it up, it drags me straight back to watching Anakin in The Phantom Menace — screaming past canyon walls at 400 MPH while trading paint and trading blows in high-stakes combat (thankfully with zero Trade Federation Senate meetings slowing things down). Trust me on this one: at $49 right now, it’s worth every single credit.

Handing out a 5/5 star rating at Tom’s Guide is roughly as rare as finding an unscalped GPU in 2026, and 007 First Light is one of the very few games to actually earn it. It’s the ultimate James Bond origin story — easily the best 007 game since GoldenEye — and as someone who had thoroughly fallen out of love with the tuxedo-and-martini routine, it somehow dragged me right back into caring about the franchise.

In his review, our very own Rory called its cinematic single-player campaign "remarkable, offering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story, packaged together with some of the best action-adventure set pieces I’ve ever experienced." That’s not just high praise — that’s basically a license to clear your weekend.

If you want to see what all the fuss is about without paying full spy-agency prices, 007 First Light is down to $34 at PlayStation right now. Shaken, stirred, or half-off — you really can't go wrong.

Yes, just like that savage parody in GTA 6, this really is the remaster of the remake of The Last of Us. At this rate, Naughty Dog is going to release a Director’s Cut for smart fridges by 2028. Chances are you’ve already survived Joel and Ellie’s road trip at least once.

That said, if you somehow missed the boat (or haven’t touched this upgraded version yet), it’s genuinely worth double-dipping. The leap in visual fidelity and animation is gorgeous, and the gameplay overhaul — complete with smarter, way more aggressive enemies that actually force you to think tactically — keeps the tension cranked to eleven.

Plus, let’s not beat around the bush: this is still the greatest story ever told in gaming. I literally have a permanent tattoo dedicated to it, so you know I’m not just saying that to hit a word count. With $41 knocked off right now, there’s zero excuse not to let it emotionally wreck you in crisp 4K.

Look, Marvel’s Wolverine might be the shiny new toy in Insomniac’s lineup, but let’s not pretend it’s the studio’s finest hour. If you ask me, the crown is a dead heat between Ratchet & Clank and this absolute masterpiece: Marvel’s Spider-Man 2.

There is genuinely nothing more therapeutic in gaming than flinging yourself across a jaw-dropping New York skyline at 90mph, casually web-slapping petty criminals into next Tuesday, and getting completely hooked by a story that actually earns its blockbuster budget.

If you somehow still haven’t swung into this one yet, it’s currently 57% off — basically highway robbery, except this time Spider-Man isn't going to stop you from getting away with it.

So it's a good news/bad news situation for the PS5 Pro. If you're looking for the absolute best way to play GTA 6, you can technically buy the console right now. And after trying it myself, trust me — this masterpiece looks truly glorious on this ultra powerful box.

The bad news? It comes at a hefty price and is pre-owned. So do with that what you will!

Just done another check around for PS5 stock and...well...it's a bit grim.

There are refurbished standard PS5 slims with the disc drive available on the PS store for $549. Elsewhere, there's nothing.

And even if there is something, like Walmart technically has the PS5 digital Slim too, it's over $1,000 now, which is crazy!

If you're picking up a console, PS store is where I'd point you right now.

Unless you’re eager to explain to your neighbors at 2 a.m. why there are police sirens and a high-speed shootout echoing through the drywall, a proper headset is the smartest way to soak in the chaos of Leonida — especially if your living room doesn’t have space for a full surround-sound setup.

My go-to picks right now come from Nacon: the RIG R5 Spear if you don’t mind a wire, and the R8 Spectre Pro if you’d rather cut the cord. Both punch well above their current sale prices, wrapping you in seriously impressive surround sound that nails everything from subtle Vice City street chatter to bone-rattling explosions.

Even better, the Black Friday discounts on both are hefty enough to leave you with spare cash for these custom faceplates — giving your cans a little extra GTA flair while you're dodging a five-star wanted level.

It's your boy — the one that likes to drive fast in video games. While I can tell you all about the best PS5 sim racing wheels, this is Black Friday weekend. Let me give you an ultimate hack to get into the hobby for less than $400.

That means the wheel, pedals and the seat. It's the Logitech G923 and PlaySeat Challenge. Of course, this wheel is not going to have the force or detail of a direct drive system. But it's a good starter kit, the seat is comfortable and it folds away really easily to store in a closet.

One of the best PS5 deals available right now is Elden Ring for just $15. This is one of the best games released in the last couple of years (assuming you're prepared for the difficulty it throws at you).

The game comes from FromSoftware, the makers of Dark Souls, Demon's Souls and other super difficult RPGs, but it's even bigger and more robust than other games from the developer. The amount of gameplay you get for only $15 is absolutely absurd. If you've somehow never played Elden Ring, this is the best time to order it.

If you like racing and you want to take the experience to the next level, the Logitech G RS50 8 Nm Racing Wheel is discounted for Black Friday on Amazon. It normally sells for $700, and it's on sale for $459.

The racing wheel is 11 inches and comes with a hub and base that seems like it'd be quite stable as you work your way around the corners. It has all the buttons you need to control the game outside of the actual races. The direct drive feature makes steering feel more precise, while trueforce increases the realism.

Since we just talked about a good deal on an NFL game, we should discuss a deal on a soccer (football) game. Or, well, the soccer game, since there really isn't any competition. EA Sports FC 27 is on sale for $30 for Black Friday, which is a great deal.

Most dedicated soccer fans probably already have this game, but if you're more of a casual soccer fan, then this is most likely the cheapest you'll see it for before next year's game drops

If you're a big fan of the NFL and somehow haven't already snagged a copy of Madden 27, you're in luck, because you can get it at a huge discount from Amazon. At $30, this is a no-brainer for anyone who enjoys a little pigskin.

This year's Madden has solid reviews, so it seems to be keeping most football fans happy. Sure, it can be a little more of the same compared to previous years, but if you want fresh rosters and some interesting gameplay tweaks, it's still worth getting, especially with this big discount.

PlayStation made its name with excellent platformers, and Astro Bot might be the best of the lot.

This PS5 exclusive is as good as a 3D Mario title, and makes smart use of the DualSense controller’s unique feature set. It also acts as a lovely stroll down memory lane for the PlayStation brand, and is well worth a look for families or anyone in need of some nostalgia.

It’s one of the best PlayStation games ever (our words), and it’s now just $37 at Amazon.

Silent Hill: Townfall is a game we called “the best Silent Hill game in 25 years”, and it’s just $29.96 right now at Amazon.

A terrifying new game in the long-running survival horror series, Townfall moves the setting to an isolated area of Scotland where the familiar fog has set in.

It's an unforgettable adventure, and essentially acts as a standalone adventure.

A chaotic co-op multiplayer shooter with more than a hint of Starship Troopers, Helldivers 2 was a viral hit when it launched in 2024.

Since then the forces of Super Earth have gained new weapons, rewards, and encountered new foes, but the core gameplay remains brilliant.

Players drop into a variety of planets to fight robots, bugs, and more, almost always accidentally dropping airstrikes on their own team.

You can spread Managed Democracy for just $30 at Walmart right now, a discount of almost ten bucks.

Yearning for a PlayStation handheld? Sony hasn’t launched one since the PlayStation Vita, but the Portal might be just what you need.

This Walmart deal nets you the Portal, as well as a handy accessories kit including a charging dock, carry case, outer shell, earbuds, and a screen protector at a $35 discount.

NBA 2K27 just launched a few weeks ago, and has a neat GTA 6 tie-in event, but it's better than half price right now. In fact, it's been reduced another couple of cents since we covered it on Thursday.

The best-looking sports sim around is under $30 for the Standard Edition on PS5. There are improvements to animations, female MyPLAYERs, and new MyCAREER Eras to explore.

Even if you're a casual basketball fan, it's worth a look at this price!

Whether you've got a PS5 or PS5 Pro, Gran Turismo 7 is one of the best-looking games on Sony hardware.

The legendary racing franchise returned in 2022, and it's only got better since then - and it’s seeing a big discount at Target.

So good-looking that you’ll want to reach out and touch the steering wheel, the game is still getting updates to include new cars, tracks, and quality-of-life features.

Our reviewer awarded it 4.5 stars out of 5 in our review, and it's an outstanding showcase for your console.

We highlighted it earlier this week, but one of the best games ever made, Elden Ring, is still discounted to the tune of 70%.

If you've picked up a console just for GTA 6 and missed out on this fantasy action-RPG, you can snag it for just $15 right now at Amazon.

The PS5 version has a colossal 96-percent positive rating on Metacritic, and if you have a great timer with it, there's also the massive Shadow of the Erdtree expansion to download to continue your adventure.

Here's a game that divides the team at Tom's Guide. Some of us love it, some of us...not so much. The consensus is it's no Spider-Man, but Logan's solo outing is still an entertaining adventure. There's the typical graphical flair you'd expect from developer Insomniac Games and plenty of blood-soaked gore.

Naturally, as a tentpole title it's been pricey up to now — but with $20 off for Black Friday, it's a much more tempting prospect if you haven't picked it up yet.

We're living in a world of remakes right now (*cough*...Zelda....*cough*), but one of the best just fell down to a price that's laughably cheap. You can currently pick up Capcom's Resident Evil 5 remake for just $13.59 right now.

You get the same iconic story, epic gunplay and nerve-jangling horror, but with some gorgeous (and gruesome) new graphics on modern-gen hardware. This is the best way to enjoy one of the strongest titles in the entire Resident Evil lineup.

It's Thanksgiving weekend, which means after the turkey is done, it's time for football. And right now you can pick up this year's Madden NFL title for less than half price at Amazon.

The retailer is offering the PS5 version of EA Sports Madden NFL 27 for just $29. This latest entry in the series includes new features like Franchise improvements and personality-led demands from players, as well as new strategies and plays.

Black Friday may be over for another year, but the deals are a long way from being done. Over the next couple of days (some folks call it Cyber Monday), I'm expecting to see plenty of deals on PS5 games and accessories continue to be available.

The PS5 console itself has been a hard get this week, and demand is still sky high. If you want the cheapest model available, I'm still seeing the base PS5 Slim on sale for $599 at GameStop.
